chunks: And also among what was narrated by ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from Abān, from Abī al-ʿAbbās, who said:

A man came to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and said, “Indeed, I have committed zina.” So the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم turned his face away from him. Then he came to him from his other side and again said the like of what he had said, so he turned his face away from him. Then he came to him a third time and said, “O Messenger of Allah, I have committed zina, and the punishment of this world is easier for me than the punishment of the Hereafter.” So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said, “Is there something wrong with your companion?” meaning madness. They said, “No.” Then he confessed against himself a fourth time, so the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ordered that he be stoned. They dug a pit for him, and when he felt the touch of the stones, he ran away swiftly. Al-Zubayr met him and struck him with the leg-bone of a camel, disabling him; then the people caught up with him and killed him. They informed the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم of that, and he said, “Why did you not leave him?” Then he said, “Had he concealed himself and then repented, that would have been better for him.”

key_terms.أَقَرَّ: he confessed or acknowledged against himself
key_terms.اسْتَتَرَ: he concealed himself; did not expose his sin publicly
key_terms.تَابَ: he repented; returned to Allah in repentance
key_terms.زَنَيْتُ: I committed zina; an admission of unlawful sexual intercourse
key_terms.عَذَابُ الدُّنْيَا: the punishment of this world; worldly legal penalty
key_terms.عَذَابِ الْآخِرَةِ: the punishment of the Hereafter; divine punishment after death
key_terms.يُرْجَمَ: that he be stoned; the ordered hadd punishment in this case

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about confessing zina, legal punishment, and repentance?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates the case of a man who repeatedly confessed to zina before the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم until the legal punishment was carried out. It also shows that concealing one’s sin and repenting sincerely to Allah is better than exposing oneself, while highlighting the seriousness of the prescribed hadd and the reality of punishment in the Hereafter.
